findings.title: ADR-0016's own table contradicts its own Case-B text and cited v1 fix (4bc292fc) for Claude Code
findings.detail: ADR-0016 Case B row text says: 'Claude Code ignores allow + updatedInput for Bash, v1 4bc292fc'. ADR-0008 r3 Q3 decision confirms: 'case B never uses allow + updatedInput.' Yet ADR-0016's own per-agent table two lines later still lists: 'Claude Code | yes | updatedInput + allow (LV1) | ...' for Case B. Git archaeology: cm-main commit 4bc292fc ('fix(hooks): claude-code Bash modify -> deny (CC ignores updatedInput.command)') is the real v1 fix being cited, and it proves updatedInput+allow does NOT work on Claude Code Bash -- it was abandoned for a hard deny precisely because CC ignores it. The table cell is now stale/wrong against the ADR's own prose and the Q3 decision.
findings.fix: Change the Claude Code Case B table cell to 'deny with rewritten command (no updatedInput, per Q3/4bc292fc)', matching the prose and ADR-0008 Q3. Remove the dangling 'LV1' label from Claude Code's row since LV1 as described (allow+updatedInput) is already known-failing, not merely unverified.

findings.title: ADR-0009's journal design depends on a Claude Code hook event (PostToolUseFailure) that does not exist in any v1 commit or ADR-0001's canonical event list
findings.detail: ADR-0009 states: 'Claude Code also registers PostToolUseFailure. Without it, failures are never recorded.' ADR-0001 (the canonical hook contract ADR) lists only four canonical events: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse -- no PostToolUseFailure. Git archaeology in cm-main: `git log --all -S 'PostToolUseFailure'` returns ONLY the two v2 docs commits (ac6a7961, 51570583) that introduce this ADR text itself -- no hook registration code, no v1 adapter, no test ever implements or exercises an event by this name. Claude Code's documented hook events are PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Notification/UserPromptSubmit/Stop/SubagentStop/PreCompact/SessionStart/SessionEnd; PostToolUse already carries success/error info in its payload. This looks like an invented event name, not a real Claude Code mechanism.
findings.fix: Either name the real mechanism (reading `tool_response.is_error`/error field inside the existing PostToolUse payload, not a separate event) and update ADR-0001's canonical event list to say so explicitly, or if a distinct event genuinely exists, cite the Claude Code doc/version where it is defined. Until resolved, the whole 'open errors' section of the compaction journal (ADR-0009 section 2) is unverified for Claude Code specifically, since error/exit_code capture is its only data source.

findings.title: ADR-0008's mcp_tool hook-type gating claim for availability detection is unverified and may not exist as a PreToolUse matcher type
findings.detail: ADR-0008 item 4 states: 'Claude Code: the PreToolUse hook is type:"mcp_tool", so it runs only while this session's server is connected; otherwise the tool runs.' Claude Code's PreToolUse hook matcher is a tool-name pattern (e.g. matching `mcp__context-mode__.*`), not a hook-level `type` discriminator like `mcp_tool`; no ADR or TECH-SPEC section cites a Claude Code doc page or version for a `type:"mcp_tool"` hook kind, and no git-archaeology evidence (commit/PR) is given for this claim the way other rows in the same table cite one. Finding #36 in REVIEW-r4a already flags `ctx_route`/mcp_tool as undocumented in any tool list; this finding is distinct -- it is about the hook **matcher mechanism itself**, which the availability-check logic (fixing #1055/#1053/#347/#173/#230) depends on.
findings.fix: Cite the exact Claude Code settings.json hook-matcher syntax being relied on (tool-name regex matcher on PreToolUse, which is the real mechanism), and correct the prose from 'type:"mcp_tool"' to the actual matcher field name; add one GP3/LV case that proves the 'server disconnected -> tool runs unblocked' path on a live Claude Code session.

findings.title: ADR-0001's canonical event list omits Stop/SubagentStop/PreCompact/SessionEnd/Notification even though downstream ADRs rely on agent-specific equivalents of them
findings.detail: ADR-0001 fixes the canonical contract to exactly 4 events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse), calling this 'the' canonical hook schema. But ADR-0009 relies on SessionStart(source=compact) replacing the need for PreCompact, and ADR-0016 case A/B/C for subagents implicitly needs to know when a subagent finishes (SubagentStop) for the live checks LV9/LV10 to assert over 'the task still finished.' Neither PreCompact nor SubagentStop is acknowledged anywhere in ADR-0001's gap table (README section 6), so a reader cannot tell whether these were considered and excluded on purpose, or simply missed.
findings.fix: Add PreCompact, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionEnd, and Notification to ADR-0001's event inventory with an explicit 'out of canonical scope, used only via the agent-specific gap table' note, so the omission reads as a decision, not an oversight.
